The text explores the dual nature of Victor Frankenstein’s act of creation through the lens of different reader backgrounds. For readers grounded in science and ethics, the narrative serves as a critique of scientific hubris, emphasizing the moral obligations that accompany technological or biological advancement. Conversely, readers with religious perspectives interpret the story as a theological warning against the transgression of divine boundaries, framing the monster’s creation as an act of "playing God." This divergence highlights how personal and cultural frameworks shape the interpretation of literary themes, particularly those involving creation and responsibility.
